1.q: וַ⁠יִּ֨מְלָךְ מֶ֔לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בֶּן יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ תַּ֗חַת כָּנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן יְה֣וֹיָקִ֔ים
1.note: Jeremiah is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

2.q: וְ⁠לֹ֥א שָׁמַ֛ע ה֥וּא וַ⁠עֲבָדָ֖י⁠ו וְ⁠עַ֣ם הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ אֶל דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה
2.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **he and his servants and the people of the land** before the information about what they **did not listen** to, so that **the words of Yahweh** follow directly. Alternate translation: [But he and his servants and the people of the land did not listen to the words of Yahweh]

2.q: וְ⁠לֹ֥א שָׁמַ֛ע ה֥וּא וַ⁠עֲבָדָ֖י⁠ו וְ⁠עַ֣ם הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ אֶל דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה
2.note: By **listen**, Jeremiah means “obey” or “pay attention.” See how you translated “listen” in 7:13. Alternate translation: [But he and his servants and the people of the land did not obey the words of Yahweh] or [But he did not obey, he and his servants and the people of the land, the instructions that Yahweh spoke]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:9.

Here, **hand** represents Jeremiah as the person through whom Yahweh spoke his words. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and was delivered by means of Jeremiah the prophet]

Even though Jeremiah is the one telling this account, he is speaking of himself in the third person as **Jeremiah the prophet**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person, here and wherever Jeremiah is named in this chapter. This also occurs in verses 3, 6, and 13. Alternate translation: [through me, Jeremiah the prophet]

3.q: אֶת יְהוּכַ֣ל בֶּן שֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֗ה וְ⁠אֶת צְפַנְיָ֤הוּ בֶן מַֽעֲשֵׂיָה֙
3.note: The words **Jehucal**, **Shelemiah**, **Zephaniah**, and **Maaseiah** are the names of men.

3.q: הִתְפַּלֶּל נָ֣א בַעֲדֵ֔⁠נוּ אֶל יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵֽי⁠נוּ
3.note: By **us**, King Zedekiah means himself and his people but not Jeremiah, to whom his messengers are speaking, so use the exclusive form of that word in your translation if your language marks that distinction. However, by **our God**, he includes Jeremiah, so use the inclusive form there if your language marks that distinction.
See how you translated the similar expression in 26:13. This also occurs in verse 7.

4.q: וְ⁠יִרְמְיָ֕הוּ בָּ֥א וְ⁠יֹצֵ֖א בְּ⁠ת֣וֹךְ הָ⁠עָ֑ם וְ⁠לֹֽא־נָתְנ֥וּ אֹת֖⁠וֹ בֵּ֥ית ה⁠כליא
4.note: Jeremiah is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

Jeremiah is using **was coming and going** as a common expression of the culture to mean “was moving about freely.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [was free to go wherever he wanted among the people]

The pronoun **they** refers to the officials who had the authority to put people in prison. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the officials had not put him in the house of imprisonment]

5.note: The author is not distinguishing **the Chaldeans** from **the ones laying siege**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make the relationship between these phrases clearer. Alternate translation: [the Chaldeans who were laying siege]
See how you translated “laying seige” in Jeremiah 32:2.

Jeremiah is using the possessive form **their report** to describe a report about the army of Pharaoh, not a report that the army itself gave. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the Chaldeans who were laying siege against Jerusalem heard the report about the army of Pharaoh]
See how you translated this name in 35:11. This also occurs in verses 8–11, 13, and 14.

6.note: See how you translated this expression in 28:12.

7.note: See how you translated this expression in 21:4.

7.q: כֹּ֤ה תֹֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה הַ⁠שֹּׁלֵ֧חַ אֶתְ⁠כֶ֛ם אֵלַ֖⁠י לְ⁠דָרְשֵׁ֑⁠נִי הִנֵּ֣ה
7.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [You shall tell the king of Judah, the one sending you to me to inquire of me, that indeed]

8.note: It might seem that the expression **burn it with fire** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [and burn it to the ground] or [and burn it]

9.note: Yahweh says **saying** to introduce an imaginary situation to help explain what the people of Judah should not say or think to themselves. Use a natural method in your language for introducing an imaginary situation. Alternate translation: [by saying or thinking]

Jeremiah is repeating forms of the verb **Going** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [The Chaldeans will surely withdraw from us]

10.q: וְ⁠נִ֨שְׁאֲרוּ בָ֔⁠ם אֲנָשִׁ֖ים מְדֻקָּרִ֑ים אִ֤ישׁ בְּ⁠אָהֳל⁠וֹ֙ יָק֔וּמוּ וְ⁠שָֽׂרְפ֛וּ אֶת הָ⁠עִ֥יר הַ⁠זֹּ֖את בָּ⁠אֵֽשׁ
10.note: Yahweh says that even **pierced men** lying wounded in their tents **would rise up and burn this city with fire**. This is an extreme statement for emphasis. Yahweh means that the Chaldeans will certainly destroy Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [and only wounded men were left among them, each in his tent, they would still certainly destroy this city]

Jeremiah is not distinguishing this **army of the Chaldeans** from another army of the Chaldeans that is fighting with the people of Judah. Jeremiah is reminding his audience that this is the very army now attacking them, so that they realize they cannot escape from it. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [the army of the Chaldeans, who are attacking you right now,]

The expression **pierced men were left** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who did the action, it would be the people of Judah, who would have wounded the Chaldeans in battle. Alternate translation: [and only wounded men remained among them]

11.note: Jeremiah is using the word translated as **And it happened** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Jeremiah is using **from the face of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because of the army of Pharaoh]

12.note: The implication is that Jeremiah was going to the land of Benjamin in order to receive something there. This could mean: (1) that Jeremiah was going to claim his share of family property in Benjamin. Alternate translation: [to claim his share of the family property there among the people] or (2) that Jeremiah was going to receive a portion of something along with the people there. Alternate translation: [to receive a portion there among the people]

13.note: The words **Irijah**, **Shelemiah**, and **Hananiah** are the names of men.

14.note: Jeremiah is using a word that expresses a strong feeling of indignation at being falsely accused. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [That is not true]
The pronoun **he** refers to Irijah, and the pronoun **him** refers to Jeremiah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [But Irijah did not listen to Jeremiah]

15.note: The word **Jonathan** is the name of a man.

16.note: The **house of the cistern** was a prison built in an underground area, and the **cells** were small rooms where prisoners were kept. If your readers would not be familiar with what these were, you could use the names of similar things that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [the prison built in a hole in the ground and to its small cells]
Here, **many days** represents “a long time.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [a long while]

17.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 21:10.

18.note: The word **you** is plural here because Jeremiah is addressing King Zedekiah along with his officials, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

18.q: מֶה֩ חָטָ֨אתִֽי לְ⁠ךָ֤ וְ⁠לַ⁠עֲבָדֶ֨י⁠ךָ֙ וְ⁠לָ⁠עָ֣ם הַ⁠זֶּ֔ה
18.note: Jeremiah is using the question form to emphasize that he has not done anything wrong. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [I have done nothing wrong against you or against your servants or against this people! So what is the reason]
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:10.

19.q: ו⁠אי⁠ו נְבִ֣יאֵי⁠כֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר נִבְּא֥וּ לָ⁠כֶ֖ם לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר לֹֽא יָבֹ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶל֙ עֲלֵי⁠כֶ֔ם וְ⁠עַ֖ל הָ⁠אָ֥רֶץ הַ⁠זֹּֽאת
19.note: Jeremiah is using the question form to emphasize that the prophets who said the king of Babylon would not come have been shown to be false. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, ‘The king of Babylon will not come against you and against this land,’ have clearly been proven false!]

19.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר לֹֽא־יָבֹ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֙ עֲלֵי⁠כֶ֔ם וְ⁠עַ֖ל הָ⁠אָ֥רֶץ הַ⁠זֹּֽאת
19.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [saying that the king of Babylon would not come against you and against this land]

20.note: Jeremiah is using **let my supplication fall to your face** as a common expression of the culture to mean “accept my request.” See how you translated the similar expression “Perhaps their supplication will fall to the face of” in 36:7. Alternate translation: [Please accept my request]

Here, **so** marks **I will not die there** as the goal or purpose of Jeremiah’s request that the king not send him back to the house of Jonathan the scribe. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

21.q: עַד תֹּ֥ם כָּל הַ⁠לֶּ֖חֶם מִן הָ⁠עִ֑יר
21.note: The implication is that the bread in the city ran out because the Chaldean army was besieging Jerusalem and no food could be brought into the city. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [until all the bread in the city was used up because the Babylonian army was besieging Jerusalem]

The **courtyard of the guard** was an enclosed area in the royal palace where the soldiers who guarded the palace were stationed and where prisoners could be kept under watch. If your readers would not be familiar with this kind of place, you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [to the courtyard where the palace guards were stationed]
